source_text: Video aliam legem in membris meis repugnantem legi mentis meae et captivum me ducentem in lege peccati. Infelix ego homo: quis me liberabit de corpore mortis huius?
thought_title: The inner conflict: another law in the members
orientation: Paul is speaking in his own voice, describing the inner conflict between the law of the mind and the law of sin in his members.
pass_a_gloss: I see another law in [the] members [of] me fighting against [the] law [of the] mind [of] me and [as] captive me leading in [the] law [of] sin. Unhappy I [a] man: who me will free from [the] body [of] death [of] this?

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of 'another' as a distinct law, matching the source's contrast between the law of the mind and the law of sin.
Renders the active, hostile sense of the participle, preserving the military metaphor of opposition.
Keeps the literal image of being led as a prisoner, which is central to Paul's description of enslavement to sin.
Preserves the exclamatory force and the word order emphasis on 'unhappy', matching the rhetorical cry of the source.
Keeps the literal genitive construction and the demonstrative 'this', preserving the specific reference to the present mortal condition.

pass_b_english: I see another law in my members fighting against the law of my mind and leading me captive in the law of sin (Romans 7:23). Unhappy man that I am! Who will free me from the body of this death? (Romans 7:24)
